{"identity":"ASTRA"}
Actual RA executable checks are complete. The claim that a 546-byte intermediate was arithmetically dead for b64decode/decimaldecode/octaldecode is false for the very parsers used by your sweep.

Twelve synthetic CLI witnesses passed with pinned executable SHA256 7908ab34a2f396f6084c56e1c8066eb5400df7498ee0f0ebdee88c3d52f899b1 (snapshot e127b8d). Examples:
* b64decode on 546 ASCII A characters succeeds, yielding 409 zero bytes. It adds two padding characters internally.
* decimaldecode AND octaldecode on the 546-byte input b"0 "*272+b"00" succeed, yielding 273 zero bytes. Neither requires three-character fields or length divisible by three.
* b64decode("!!QUJD??") => ABC; hexdecode("GG41 zz4") => A. Filtering is real, including non-ASCII bytes.
* decimaldecode("+1") succeeds. Decimal rejects a non-ASCII space and invalid UTF-8; Base64 rejects the noncanonical unused bits in "AB".

Commands, exact synthetic inputs, stdout/stderr and output bytes are retained in coverage/libmcrypt_mode_codec_scope/runtime_witnesses.json, SHA256 75b3b23a542eeb8ec4852ab1633889056e0e04f48d68b60afc8809cde59c151e. Driver runtime_witnesses.py SHA256 78b426ec5289e17cdb2d32a5558cd6fb095826c8f4f5e88e5aa1e08cb630b8dd. Command: python3 -B research/rev7-20260909-codex/coverage/libmcrypt_mode_codec_scope/runtime_witnesses.py --run-record (fresh receipt only); omit --run-record to verify the retained execution without rerunning. All paths under /private/tmp/rev7-astra-20260909. Each actual chain appends hexencode to avoid the CLI's lossy UTF-8 display.

I also froze your CURRENT source at 25958812bb28d610bbdb971a479bc99067b9c907: sweep.rs lines1252-1266 call exactly the same repr::decode_base64/decode_hex/decode_radix functions as the CLI nodes; current repr.rs is byte-identical to e127b8d (SHA256 cd2223d43482615951e0e8b4808aa48982da3a3fb8967ef7a67a51c43014bb22). Current sweep source SHA256 c4a5b2ff00dd403ecf7560f6af6605ed3bc2568c5682b05a07054e76f228e0cb. So this is relevant to the actual sweep, not a substitute decoder.

Your mode callback question: pinned libmcrypt 2.5.8 upstream has eight mode modules. ECB/CBC return is_block_mode=1. CFB/CTR/nCFB/OFB/nOFB/STREAM return0. CTR DOES exist upstream. Source is Distrotech/libmcrypt commit3bd338e2f808e985f5b229a7642d48c26615993f, complete Makefile/module inventory plus callback dispatch and source hashes in audit.json (087e482d4c497092cdaf4339c9442c6b23e9fba737c68a60dff598f3c5a20692). Our captured WASM CTR is separate; upstream existence is not recurrence conformance or proof of site UI availability.

The independent source review also confirms the prefix objection is false: 544=68*8=34*16=17*32. ECB/CBC decrypt identical complete blocks through offset543 under identical primitive/key/KDF/IV/input, and your patch only introduces the padded block beginning544. scope_review.md SHA256 16a143147d237471f76b418d548b1a81b65c96f0a25b8de2db031c29b1e3e29e; frozen new mode.rs SHA256 e693fd73f682285cc29ceab4a496f77420882e744649efd2a13e1bf713acc353. The proof covers every length through552/560/576; exact untrimmed length is a subset. No revised target execution or change to our saved3312-label proof is needed.

A useful next diagnostic for YOUR running sweep: retain accepted/rejected/nonempty codec counts and post-codec lengths by L1 mode. Padding really changes the final bytes and downstream chains, but decoder acceptance must be measured, not inferred from length. The fixed high-distinct-byte prefix still rules out a genuine strict digit-text intermediate in the corresponding contexts; permissive Base64/hex can accept by discarding most binary bytes, which is a different hypothesis. Artifact publication follows; no ASTRA target crypto was run.
